sources.title: R432-150, Nursing Care Facility — Utah Administrative Code
sources.notes:
adminrules.utah.gov is a Next.js App Router application. The Office of Administrative Rules rebuilt it and retired the whole /api/public/ API this recipe was built on: the old getHTML address now answers 404 (HTTP 400 on one of them), and so does the human /public/rule/<ref>/Current%20Rules address (FA-Q-20261124-03, diagnosed 2026-11-24; the licensure mobility half is FA-Q-20261126-02). This address is the rule's own human page, keyed by ruleId.

WHY THE EXTRACTOR IS next-flight AND NOT html-text. /Rule/<ruleId> answers 200 to plain curl, but the rule text is not in the served DOM: it sits inside a <script> element as an escaped HTML document of absolutely-positioned DOCX-conversion spans, and extract_html drops script nodes. A repoint to this address with html-text was tried on 2026-11-24 and captured 208 characters of site navigation -- worse than the 404, because it looks like a capture that succeeded. next-flight reassembles the RSC flight payload from the page's self.__next_f.push calls and hands it to the same extract_html, so the document arrives exactly as the retired endpoint delivered it. Measured 2026-11-27 against this packet: byte-identical for R432-150 (81,947 chars) and R414-504 (13,232), and 0.9985 for R410-14, whose difference is the amendment below rather than any loss in extraction.

THE VERSION-PINNING HAZARD IS GONE, AND THE WITNESS CHANGES ROLE. The old address pinned a version GUID, so an amendment would have kept returning the superseded rule while every check passed -- the failure this project exists to prevent, and the reason the witness source was added. /Rule/<ruleId> is keyed by the rule's identity instead, so it always serves the current text and cannot go stale. The witness is still required, for the other half of the job: it records which version this capture holds, so an amendment shows as drift and a session reads it deliberately rather than finding the text changed under it.

sources.title: Skilled nursing facility-initiated discharge appeal form — Utah Division of Aging and Adult Services (PDF)
sources.source_date: form dated 11.7.23 in its own filename
sources.notes: Re-based 2026-09-04. The address the 2026-09-01 capture recorded, .../SNF-Discharge-Appeal-Form.pdf, now returns an nginx 404: the department renamed the file in place, appending its own revision date, and nothing announced the move. Found again by reading the Long Term Care Ombudsman page, which still links it. Verified before re-basing: all 8 quotations this page draws from the form appear verbatim in the renamed file, so it is the same document under a new name rather than a new form.

sources.title: Hearings — Medicaid — Utah Department of Health and Human Services
sources.notes: Cloudflare hides this page's contact address behind a client-side script. The 2026-09-01 capture left the placeholder text in the packet because curl cannot run it; decode_cfemail in the shared capture reader resolves it, and this source now yields utmedicaidhearings@utah.gov as the department publishes it.

sources.title: Medicaid Fair Hearings — Utah Department of Health and Human Services
sources.notes: The same office's contact page published on a second department domain, carried because the two are not word-for-word identical. Same Cloudflare obfuscation and same resolution as source 3.

sources.title: Utah Medicaid Provider Manual, Section I: General Information, chapter 5-4 Hearings and Administrative Review (PDF)
sources.source_date: Updated September 2026, as the chapter's own footer states (was Updated July 2026 as of the 2026-09-04 capture)
sources.notes: The 2026-09-01 capture sliced this chapter by hand from a 139-page manual. Pages 55 to 57 are the printed range that chapter occupies and contain the standing text exactly; a range is reproducible where a hand slice is not. The chapter heading also appears on pages 4 and 134, in the table of contents and in a later cross-reference, which is why the range is pinned rather than searched for by heading.

sources.title: Long Term Care Ombudsman — Aging & Adult Services, Utah Department of Health and Human Services
sources.notes: The 2026-09-01 capture had to render this page in a browser and read document.body.innerText, because every listed address was a Cloudflare placeholder to curl — recorded then as a last-resort transport, not independently re-verifiable by an automated pass. decode_cfemail removes that need: curl now yields the addresses the department publishes, and this source is ordinary again.

sources.title: Ombudsman Locations — Aging & Adult Services, Utah Department of Health and Human Services
sources.notes: Re-based 2026-09-04: the recorded address, /ombudsman-locations, 301-redirects here. Same browser-transport history and same resolution as source 6; the regional ombudsman roster's addresses now decode under curl.

sources.title: R432-150 rule metadata — Utah Office of Administrative Rules (version witness for source 1)
sources.notes:
Not a source the page quotes. Repointed 2026-11-27 with its rule text (FA-Q-20261124-03): the old /api/public/rule/<ref>/undefined/Current%20Rules address died with the rest of /api/public/. /api/ruleVersion/<ruleId> is a better witness than the address it replaces and is curl-reachable now. It is keyed by ruleId -- the rule's identity, stable across amendments -- and returns that one rule's whole version history, each entry carrying its ruleTypeName, effectiveDateRange and htmlName. So it changes when this rule is amended and at no other time, where the old address was keyed by rule number and the title-wide alternative (/api/titleRules/<titleId>) would move whenever any rule in the title did.

Its role is no longer to catch a stale pin -- source 1 is keyed by ruleId and cannot pin a version any more -- but to record which version of R432-150 this capture holds, so an amendment is visible as drift instead of arriving silently inside the rule text.

THIS SOURCE CHANGED DOCUMENT WITH THE REPOINT. It had been pinned to GUID 73994768-4705-4e78-bf9e-3167834a0136, which the witness now lists as the SUPERSEDED version of R410-14 for 09/19/2025 - 10/13/2026; the current version is ee2be259-9bb8-49e1-9dd6-1fc5b11dccaf, effective 10/14/2026. So this recipe had been quoting a superseded rule since 2026-10-14, which is exactly the failure the witness was added to catch -- it did catch it, and the 404 is why nobody saw it. The amendment: "the department's executive director" becomes "the department's commissioner" in three places, the authority citation moves from Subsection 26B-1-202(1) to 26B-1-202(2)(a) and from 42 CFR 431 Subpart E (2025) to (2026), and the KEY footer's Date of Last Change moves from September 19, 2025 to October 14, 2026. Nothing else differs but whitespace and hyphenation.
